intro: Notion for students on Mac works well once you pick the right plan and build one planner. Start by checking whether your school email qualifies for the Education Plan, then make one page for each course. This guide covers the plan limits, the Mac shortcuts, and the places Notion gets slow.

The Free plan keeps page history for 7 days and caps each upload at 5 MB.

Split big databases by semester, and keep offline views to 50 rows or fewer.

blocks.text: What Notion does well for students on Mac

Notion is a page and database app. You write notes on a page, then turn a set of pages into a table, board, calendar or gallery. For students, that means one place for lectures, readings, deadlines and grades. Students usually build a semester planner, class notes, an assignment and exam tracker, or a shared page for a group project. Those four jobs cover most of what people do with it.

The part that trips people up is the blank page. A 2sync review says the blank-canvas approach "can feel overwhelming if you just want to jot down a quick thought." That is one reviewer's view. Treat it as a warning about setup time. Start with one template and one database, then add more only when you need them.
Free plan or Education Plan: check your limits first

Check your plan before you build anything. Notion's Education help page says the Education Plan is free for individual students at accredited colleges listed in the World Higher Education Database. You sign in with a school email that is your main account email. Each school email can claim the plan once, for one workspace with one member.

The plan is not permanent. To stay on it, you verify student status once a year with your school email. If you skip that, the workspace and its content move to the Free Plan. K-12 students and educators are not eligible. Set a calendar reminder for the verification date on the day you sign up.

blocks.title: Two Notion pages disagree
blocks.text: Notion's pricing page says Plus is free for students with a one-member limit when you sign up with a school email. The Education help page describes a separate free plan. Read both on the day you sign up, then confirm the plan name inside the app.

Check file sizes too. The Free plan caps each uploaded file at 5 MB. Lecture recordings and scanned readings often go over that. Save a smaller copy of the PDF with Preview, or link to the file from your school's drive instead of uploading it to Notion.
Set up Notion for students on Mac in one evening

items: Install the Notion desktop app from notion.com, then sign in with your school email if you plan to claim the Education Plan.
Open the student starter pack linked from the Notion for Education page, then duplicate the planner you want.
Create one page per course. Put the course code in the title, such as BIO 201 Notes, so search finds it fast.
Make one database called Assignments with three properties: Due, Status and Course.
Add a calendar view to the Assignments database, so each due date shows on its day.
Turn on the desktop beta if you want lighter tabs. Go to Settings > Preferences > Desktop beta. You need app version 7.39.0 or later.
Add your planner page to Favorites in the sidebar, then close the pages you do not use this week.

blocks.text: Mac keyboard shortcuts for Notion that matter in class

Notion's shortcut list uses ⌘ on Mac where Windows uses Ctrl. Content creation uses ⌘⌥ on Mac and Ctrl+Shift on Windows and Linux. That one rule explains most of the confusion when you switch machines. Open the Keyboard shortcuts page in Notion Help for the full list, because the list changes.

items: ⌘⇧ click selects whole blocks. On Windows, the same selection is Alt+Shift+click.
⌃⌘Space opens the emoji picker. Use it to put a course icon on each page.
⌘⌥ plus a key creates content. Check the list for the exact key before you rely on it.
⌘Z undoes and ⇧⌘Z redoes, the same as in most Mac apps.
⌘F finds text on the page you are reading.

blocks.text: Learn three shortcuts first. Add more only when you repeat the same task twice in a week. A short list you use beats a long list you forget by midterm.
Keep a student database fast on a Mac

Large databases slow down. A 2sync review says Notion can struggle when it loads big databases with many relations, embeds and media. Students hit this when one database holds every assignment from every course since first year. That database gets heavy fast.

Split the work by semester. Keep one Assignments database per term, not one for your whole degree. Store large media in the page that needs it, not in each database row. Filter each view to the current term, so Notion loads fewer rows.

Offline use has a hard edge. One review states that only the first 50 database rows per view download for offline use. AI, automations and embeds need a connection. If you work on a train, limit the view to 50 rows or fewer, then open the page while you have signal and check it works offline before you travel.
Offline, export and file size limits

Exports lose layout. The 2sync review says exports do not always rebuild complex layouts, synced blocks and embeds in another app. Export a copy of anything you will hand in, then open that copy in the target app before you submit. Lab reports with tables and charts need this check most.

Page history is your safety net, but it has a window. The Free plan keeps page history for 7 days. The Education Plan keeps it for 30 days. If you rewrote a paragraph last Tuesday and want it back, check page history soon. Waiting more than a week on the Free plan means the older draft is gone.
The desktop beta and tabs on Mac

Notion's desktop beta for Mac and Windows makes tabs faster and lighter. It needs desktop app version 7.39.0 or later. Turn it on under Settings > Preferences > Desktop beta. Notion says the beta is still a work in progress, and that a few things have rough edges.

Two rough edges matter for students. The tab bar is sometimes hidden in full-screen views, which hurts if you work full screen during lectures. AI Meeting Notes also has recording-indicator issues. Test one session before you rely on it for a recorded lecture.

Notion's 3.6 release notes, dated July 1, 2026, list External Agents, HTML blocks, Outlook connections and model updates. They describe no Mac-specific menu or sidebar changes. If a menu item moved on your Mac, the release notes do not explain why.
Mistakes students make in Notion

items: Building the system instead of using it. Hours spent on icons and colors are hours with no reading done.
Nesting pages many levels deep. Flat pages with clear course titles are easier to search.
Keeping deadlines in a page instead of a database. A page does not sort itself by due date.
Submitting a Notion export without opening it first. Check tables and embeds in the final app.
Missing the yearly check on the Education Plan. Set the reminder for the day you verify.
Adding a large group of guests late. Check the guest limit before a club or project grows.

blocks.text: Templates to start from, and what they cost in time

Notion's student page highlights a student planner, a club home, a habit tracker, a website template and job-application templates. They all link to one starter pack. A 2026 Bullet roundup names Student Dashboard, Assignment and Exam Tracker, Class Notes, Pomodoro Study Timer, Cornell Notes System, Grade Calculator and Course Schedule. The roundup gives no usage numbers, so judge each template by whether you will open it next week.

Pick one template per job. For class notes, try the Cornell layout on one course for two weeks. If you do not reread those pages, switch to a plain page. A template is only useful if you open it again. The best template is the one you open on Monday.
A worked example from lecture to quiz

Say your biology lecture ends on Tuesday and the quiz is on Friday. Open the course page. Add a heading with the lecture date. Write the main points under it. Then add the quiz to Assignments with the Friday due date and the status Not started.

Open the calendar view filtered to biology. You see the quiz on Friday at a glance. Change the status as you go, from Not started to Drafting to Ready. A status column tells you more than a checkbox does, because it shows where each task stands.

If you want to talk through the lecture while you walk, hold fn and dictate your recap into the page. Dictation writes clean text at the cursor in any app. Your notes stay in Notion, next to the quiz they are for.
Deadlines, Notion Calendar and Apple Calendar

Notion's student page highlights Notion Calendar for deadlines. Keep due dates in your Assignments database, then show that database as a calendar. The calendar view works well for a term. Apple Calendar still works for class times if you already rely on it.
Give every assignment one due date and one status. Status values such as Not started, Drafting and Submitted tell you what to do next. A status column shows the whole term without opening each page.
Group projects, sharing and publishing

Notion's student page says you can share pages with collaborators for group projects and club events. It also highlights one-click website publishing. On the Education Plan, a workspace allows up to 100 guests, and page history runs 30 days. Those limits matter when a team edits the same lab report all week.

Give each page one owner. Add an Owner property to the database, then write the rules at the top of the page: who edits which section, and by when. Groups that skip this step end up with three versions of the same conclusion.
Publish only what you want public. A published page is readable by anyone with the link. Check the sharing settings before you paste a link into a group chat.
Where Lazur fits while you work in Notion

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a button is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click for you. It does not edit files or operate other apps. It is not a plugin or add-in for Notion, and there is no partnership between Lazur and Notion. Think of it as a friend who knows Macs sitting next to you while you do the clicking.
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation works well for lecture recaps and draft paragraphs. You still read and check the text before you submit anything.

Privacy matters with coursework. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer your question, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Next steps for students on Mac

Pick your plan first. Then build one planner page, one Assignments database and one notes page for your current course. Test offline use, export and a file upload before your first big deadline, not during it.

For the wider study setup, read the [Google Docs for students on Mac](/for/students/google-docs) guide if you write essays in Docs. If you keep drifting during long sessions, read [losing focus while studying on a laptop](/for/students/problems/losing-focus-while-studying-on-a-laptop). For Lazur's notes on Notion, see [Notion help with Lazur](/apps/notion).
When you are ready, start on the [download page](/download). The Lazur trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card.

faq.question: Is Notion free for students on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, the Free plan covers basic notes and planning. It keeps page history for 7 days and caps each uploaded file at 5 MB. Individual students at accredited colleges can also claim the Education Plan with a school email. Check the plan name in the app after you sign up, because Notion's two pages describe the student plan differently.

faq.question: How do I keep the Education Plan after my first year?
faq.answer: Verify your student status once a year with your school email. If you skip the check, the workspace and its content move to the Free Plan. Set a reminder for the verification date so the move does not catch you off guard.

faq.question: Does Notion work offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Only partly. A 2sync review says only the first 50 database rows per view download for offline use. AI, automations and embeds need a connection. Open your pages while online before a trip, then check them with the connection off.

faq.question: Why is Notion slow on my Mac?
faq.answer: Large databases with many relations, embeds and media are the usual cause, according to a 2sync review. Split one big database into one per semester and filter each view. You can also try the desktop beta under Settings > Preferences > Desktop beta, which needs app version 7.39.0 or later.

faq.question: Can Lazur do my Notion work for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur answers questions about your screen, points at things, guides you one click at a time and drafts text. It does not click for you or edit files. You still write, check and submit your own work.

faq.question: Where do I find the full list of Notion shortcuts for Mac?
faq.answer: Open the Keyboard shortcuts page in Notion Help. It uses ⌘ on Mac where Windows uses Ctrl, and content creation uses ⌘⌥ on Mac. Check the page before you rely on a specific key, because the list changes.
